Look, Cover, Write, Check: spelling practice that works (England, UK schools)

Look, Cover, Write, Check is the routine many primary schools in England use for weekly spellings. It takes about five minutes a day. This page adds the one thing paper can't: hearing the word.

The steps

  1. Look. Read the word aloud, then look at it closely. Notice the tricky part, such as a silent letter or an unexpected group of vowels. Tap hear to listen again in a British voice.
  2. Cover. Cover the word with your hand or a piece of paper, so your child can't see it.
  3. Write. Ask your child to write the word from memory, saying it quietly as they write.
  4. Check. Uncover the word and check it letter by letter. Right? Tick it. Wrong? Circle the part that went wrong, then do the whole routine once more.
Try it with a few words

British voice from your own device; nothing is sent anywhere.

because people friend beautiful busy children

Why it works

Writing a word from memory is harder than copying it, and that effort is what helps it stick. Checking straight away means a mistake is caught before it is practised.

How long, how often

Five or six words a session, a few minutes a day, beats one long evening. Come back to the tricky words a few days later.

Make it a little easier or harder

Younger children can trace the first try, or write only the tricky part. Older children can use the word in a sentence after the check.
